messages:
Maria G: Heads up — seeing a short-lived spike in GPU interruption_rate for the mixed-eu-west3 pool around 00:28 UTC. dashboard shows a 5x jump for ~3m then back to baseline. wondering if alerts are too sensitive or if this is real churn. :eyes:

Aj Patel: can you paste the metric window? is that eviction_rate or interruption_count?

Maria G: interruption_rate (per-minute). here's a screenshot clip pasted to the thread (inline). raw query: `sum(rate(instance_gpu_evictions_total{pool=~\"mixed-eu-west3.*\"}[1m])) by (zone)`

Kevin L: hmm, 3m blips are noise-y. current alert: `for: 1m` and threshold 0.02 evictions/s per 100 GPUs. maybe bump to `for: 5m` or add a rate-of-change filter.

Olivia K: we tuned aggressive thresholds last quarter to catch outages quickly but that did cause noisy pages. If this is short-lived and not correlated with SLO errors, we should debounce.

Maria G: what confuses me — the dashboard shows concurrent pod reschedules increased slightly, but 95th latency for generation pipelines didn't move. so user impact = none in this window.

Monitoring Bot: alert fired: `EVictionSpike_mixed_eu-west3` at 00:28:34 (severity: medium) — route: eng-infra-oncall

SRE Bot: correlated notes: recent cluster autoscaler rollout in eu-west3 at 00:20 UTC. pods were drained/rebalanced on new nodes. possible cause: batch drain + preemptible churn.

Aj Patel: suggestion: change the alert to 2 conditions: 1) `interruption_rate` sustained 5m AND 2) `pod_restarts` > baseline*1.5 over same window. that should reduce noise from infra churn.

Kevin L: agree. also add a short-term suppression when we detect a control-plane rolling event tag (we emit `cluster_rollout=true`). i can draft the alert rule.

Maria G: +1. can we also add a runbook link to the alert text so oncall knows to check autoscaler events and node drain logs?

Kevin L: working on a rule draft:
```
- alert: GPUInterruptionSustained
  expr: sum(rate(instance_gpu_evictions_total{pool=~\"mixed-eu-west3.*\"}[5m])) by (zone) > 0.015
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-interruption
    summary: "Sustained GPU interruptions in mixed-eu-west3"
```

Aj Patel: add an additional `unless` clause for `cluster_rollout` tag, something like `unless cluster_rollout == 1` or silence automatically when rollout label present.

Olivia K: small ask — make the rule return non-page severity (ticket) if user-facing latency SLOs are within tolerance. we can use the SLO exporter: `slo:latency_error_ratio` as a gate.

Maria G: good idea. low user impact => ticket. sustained + SLO breach => page.

Kevin L: i'll open a quick PR with the alert rule + runbook link + suppression. PR: https://git.redwood/inframon/pulls/457 (WIP). tagging @Aj for review.

Aj Patel: will review. also propose adding a short-lived metric `eviction_burst_count` to help detect bursty noise so alerting can be tuned without losing sensitivity for real capacity shortages.

SRE Bot: note: automated mitigation exists — fallback routing to dedicated pools if sustained interruptions > threshold for 15m. ensure routing config is visible in runbook.

Olivia K: can we add a Grafana panel that overlays autoscaler events + eviction spikes? that made triage much faster last time.

Maria G: yes — added to dashboard ticket: https://issues.redwood/internal/INFRA-893. I'll add the sample query and panel layout.

Kevin L: quick patch planned: change `for: 1m` -> `for: 5m`, add `slo` gating, and add `cluster_rollout` suppression. if no objections i'll merge after Aj approves.

Aj Patel: no objections. :+1:

Maria G: thanks all. we'll monitor for a few days and revisit if pages reappear. filing a post-check note in runbook after merge.

Monitoring Bot: alert cleared: `EVictionSpike_mixed_eu-west3` at 00:31:12

Olivia K: :white_check_mark: closing loop — no user-facing impact for that spike. leaving the tweak on staging to bake for 24h.
